newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - HCIA in freefall.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - HCIA in freefall.

text.p: Shares in HCIA Inc declined sharply in a pre-open selloff Tuesday sparked by the company's announcement last night that third quarter earnings are expected to be $0.10 to $0.15 per share, excluding a $41.2 million acqusition-related charge.
Ahead of the open, HCIA shares initially fell to 38 from 60, then continued lower to 32 as investors abandoned the stock, traders said.
Analysts had expected HCIA to post earnings per share of $0.29 in each the third and fourth quarters.
Analysts had expected HCIA to post earnings per share of $0.29 in each of the third and fourth quarters.
Last year, HCIA posted earnings per share of $0.19 in the third quarter and $0.18 in the fourth quarter.
In the fourth quarter, the company said it expects to report earnings per share in the $0.15 to $0.20 range.
The HCIA news also weighed on the share price of HBO & Co, which like HCIA is a provider of healthcare management software.
HBO shares fell 3-1/4 to 63-1/2 preceding the market open, traders said.
Further eroding investor confidence in HCIA was a Merrill Lynch downgrade to near-term neutral from buy, according to market sources.

A warning of declining earnings also knocked down shares in Xilinx Inc, which said after Monday's market close that it expects net income and revenue for the second quarter ended September 28 to be below those in the prior quarter.
The shares traded at 31-1/4, down from 34 before the open, a slide facilitated by Goldman Sach lowering its Xilinx 1996 and 1997 earnings estimates, traders said.
Xilinx said net income before a $5 million pre-tax charge is expected to be about $0.30 per share versus $0.41.

According to First Call, analysts expected the company to report a profit for the second quarter of fiscal 1997 of $0.38 a share. Xilinx reported year-ago second quarter profits of $28.8 million or $0.37 a share on revenues of $141.2 million.
Also, it said it expects revenues to be about 12 to 13 percent below the first quarter level of $150.2 million.
Selling in Xilinx spread to Altera Corp, which slipped 1-5/8 to 49, according to traders.
